_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.mathematical.mathematical` declares 15 mutation kinds, of which 14 address a graph and a point cloud that are no longer persisted fields but composed children, and one (`change-coefficient`) edits the labelled equation AST. Semio-NATIVE, no oracle; the decision below records both the declined candidates and the thinness of the committed vectors for the 13 graph/geometry kinds.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: `s.mathematical.mathematical` is a semio-NATIVE artifact. Its persisted body is three composed child handles (`notation` → `s.stdio.semio.text`, `results` → `s.stdio.semio.table`, `computed` → `s.stdio.semio.value`) plus ONE plain field, `equation`: a labelled expression AST whose `EquationNodeLabel` allocator only ever increases, so an address survives edits that a positional path would not. Both candidate families were surveyed and DECLINED. `petgraph` is the credible Rust graph library, but it models a graph as an in-memory container — it cannot read `.dsl.semio`, it has no notion of node labels, positions, an algorithm selector or a directedness flag, and it has no editing vocabulary whose results could be compared with ours. On the algebra side an external CAS is likewise the wrong instrument: `symbolica` is commercially licensed and cannot be linked here, and the small expression crates (`meval`, `evalexpr`) EVALUATE a string rather than exposing an authored, labelled AST, so none of them can adjudicate `change-coefficient`, which edits a numbered term in place. Evidence is the fifteen committed specification vectors plus the inverse law — and, recorded here rather than hidden, that evidence is thin for thirteen of the fifteen kinds: the graph and point-cloud verbs address collections that live in composed children the fixtures cannot resolve, so nine of them carry `rejected` vectors (`mutation.target-missing`, `mutation.duplicate-id`) and four carry `applied`-but-`mutation.no-op` vectors. Only `change-coefficient` and `insert-point` carry a forward, observable vector.
